panels.description: Role and synchronization health per availability replica. Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.
panels.title: Replica State

panels.description: Per database replica: synchronization state, suspension, lag and queues. Queues are absent while data movement is suspended (SQL Server reports NULL). Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.
panels.title: Database Replica State
Data Movement & Sync State
panels.description: Red = suspended / not synchronizing. A suspended secondary makes the log send queue disappear and the primary's log grow (see Log Used). Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.

targets.expr: max by (sqlserver_instance, db_name) (sqlserver_database_log_used_percent) and on (db_name) max by (db_name) (sqlserver_hadr_database_synchronization_state{ag_name=~"$ag"})

panels.title: Log Used (AG databases)
panels.description: Transaction log usage of databases in the selected AGs, per instance. The log cannot be truncated while a secondary is behind or suspended.

panels.title: Log Send Queue
panels.description: Log not yet sent to the secondary. Absent while data movement is suspended. Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Redo Queue
panels.description: Log received but not yet redone on the secondary. Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Secondary Lag
panels.description: Seconds the secondary is behind the primary, as reported on the primary (SQL Server 2016+). Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.
